name: Generic Supermarket
description: Default RETINA store: a mid-size US supermarket built from RETINA's own datasets. Illustrative - not any real retailer.

labels.catalog_file: REAL_OBSERVED prices (Open Prices) + PUBLIC_STATISTIC popularity (Instacart) + ESTIMATED fields - see catalog columns. Cleaned by loaders/clean_catalog.py: wrong name matches moved by their real Open Food Facts category, pack sizes added, duplicates merged, promotions capped at 50%
labels.simulation: SIMULATED - run settings chosen by us; n_shoppers 'auto' = the NPC pool is sized so its trips match the traffic schedule
labels.traffic.real_shoppers_per_week: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - FMI Supermarket Facts: 13,583 average weekly transactions per US supermarket (2018). A supercenter is busier: Walmart 10-K FY2026 says ~280 million customers a week over ~10,900 stores = ~25,700 per store (includes online, so an upper bound)
labels.traffic.weekend_vs_weekday: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - USDA ERS from the American Time Use Survey 2014-17: 16% of people grocery shop on an average weekend day vs 13% on a weekday (16/13 = 1.23)
labels.traffic.hourly_curve: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - Instacart order hours (ONLINE orders, 2017), cut to opening hours. Check: ATUS says in-store weekday peaks are 11am-1pm and 3-4pm. Put real door-counter numbers in hourly_counts (a typical weekday, e.g. {"7": 40, "8": 90, ...}) to use those instead (REAL_OBSERVED)
labels.traffic.open_hours: ESTIMATED - 7:00 to 23:00, a common supermarket schedule
labels.traffic.npc_scale: SIMULATED - our choice: 0.1 = one NPC stands for 10 real shoppers (100 real at 10 am -> about 10 NPCs)
labels.shoppers.price_sensitivity_spread: ESTIMATED - spread chosen by us, not measured
labels.shoppers.weekday_habit: ESTIMATED - habit strength chosen by us
labels.shoppers.instacart_day0: ESTIMATED - Instacart does not say which weekday day 0 is; we assume Sunday
labels.shoppers.history_trips: TUNED - each NPC starts with about 6 past trips of purchases, drawn from what real shoppers re-buy (Instacart prior orders); 6 chosen on the TUNING half of the held-out baskets
labels.shoppers.aisle_affinity / mission_sharpn: TUNED - shopping missions use real Instacart aisle pairs (PUBLIC_STATISTIC, prior orders); these two strengths were tuned on the TUNING half of the held-out baskets (realism.py); the final score uses the other half
labels.shoppers.needs: Needs-driven shopping (step 14). PUBLIC_STATISTIC inputs from Instacart prior orders (loaders/trip_needs.py): trip size vs days since the last trip, how much trip size swings, and per aisle how many trips pass before the same product is bought again. TUNED (on prior-order statistics, before the held-out test): home_factor = a product lasts home_factor x real re-buy trips x the NPC's own days between trips; habit_power = inside an aisle, the product bought most becomes a habit (times bought ^ power); need_tries = usual products checked for one that ran out; repeat_boost = re-buy chance x 1.05 to keep the real repeat share. budget: extras stop once a week's food money (household budget) is spent on this trip; needed items are still bought
labels.households.size_shares: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - EIA Residential Energy Consumption Survey 2024, table HC9.1: 132.5 million US homes by number of members (5 = five or more)
labels.households.food_at_home_*: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2022 (tables 1400 by household size, 1101 by income quintile), moved to the simulated year's prices with the real CPI-U food at home index
labels.households.kids_*: ESTIMATED - from BLS CE 2022 average children under 18 per household size (2 people 0.1, 3 people 0.6, 4 people 1.5, 5+ people 2.7)
labels.households.link_*: ESTIMATED - strength of the links (rank correlations): basket size <-> household size, household size <-> income, income <-> price sensitivity (negative = poorer is more sensitive)
labels.pricing.promo_weekly_prob: ESTIMATED - promotion frequency chosen by us
labels.pricing.price_elasticity: ESTIMATED - based on Bijmolt et al. 2005 meta-analysis (about -2.6)
labels.pricing.ref_price_memory: ESTIMATED - memory speed chosen by us (Kalyanaram & Winer 1995 concept)
labels.pricing.loss_aversion: ESTIMATED - moderate value; evidence mixed (Bell & Lattin 2000)
labels.pricing.reference_share: ESTIMATED - share of the price effect that comes from comparing with remembered prices (fades as memory adapts); the rest is permanent
labels.pricing.category_response: ESTIMATED - walk-away strength when a whole aisle feels pricier; 0.2 makes aisle-level demand far less price-sensitive than single products (category vs brand elasticity)
labels.promotion_response: ESTIMATED - TUNED so the promo bump splits ~1/3 each (Van Heerde et al. 2004)
labels.operations.lead_time_days / safety_days: ESTIMATED - TUNED so ~8% of wanted items are out of stock (Gruen et al. 2002)
labels.operations.fresh_min_sales: ESTIMATED - assortment rule chosen by us
labels.operations.shelf_life_days: ESTIMATED - typical shelf lives chosen by us
labels.operations.gross_margin / default_margin: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - AgMRC citing NaveoCommerce 2023 (industry rule of thumb)
labels.out_of_stock_reactions: PUBLIC_STATISTIC - Gruen, Corsten & Bharadwaj 2002 (survey of 71,000 shoppers)
labels.floor: ESTIMATED - a typical supermarket layout (fresh food on the walls, packaged goods on racks) and walking, picking and checkout times chosen by us; not measured in any real store
